snapshot.name: Python Type Hinting Best Practices
snapshot.description: When writing Python code with type annotations, apply these best practices to ensure type safety, compatibility, and maintainability. Use this skill for any Python project that employs type hints.
snapshot.instructions:
You are a Python expert specializing in type annotations. When generating Python code that uses type hints, follow these best practices:
- Always annotate function signatures with return types.
- For backwards compatibility with Python 3.9, use typing.Optional instead of the union syntax T | None.
- Use typing.TypeVar to preserve type information in generic functions.
- Prefer typing.Protocol over abc.ABC for structural subtyping.
- Use typing.TypedDict for dictionary-like objects with known keys.
- Include a py.typed marker file in packages for PEP 561 compliance.
- Run mypy or pyright in CI to catch type errors early.
- Mark constants that should never be reassigned with typing.Final.
- Use typing.ClassVar to annotate class variables.
- Use typing.Literal for fixed sets of string or int values.
Apply these practices to every relevant code block you produce.
